claims: The documented upstream IRX import-link structure uses a jump-to-return-address instruction followed by a 16-bit immediate whose source and target registers are both zero; the link terminator is a zero entry and library version is 16-bit.
The parser requires the measured/documented corpus import stub form (jr $ra word 0x03e00008; ADDIU opcode 9 with rs=rt=0), an all-zero two-word terminator, and zero version high bits.
Every one of 748 observed import stubs and 166 terminators across these 24 modules matches those encodings.

evidence.text: Screened public frno7/iopmod include/iopmod/irx.h struct irx_import_link declaration: comment says jr is an unconditional MIPS I jump to return-address instruction; li is a 16-bit load-immediate pseudo-instruction whose imm is imported link index and whose rt and rs are $0. struct irx_import_library says the zero field is always zero; link array has terminating entry zero; version is 16-bit BCD. Source excerpt was screened earlier; recommendation was review because an ordinary C struct/comment excerpt had nonzero injection probability. Manual inspection found no agent-directed content.
Screened public frno7/iopmod include/iopmod/asm/irx.h declares SHT_IOPMOD 0x70000080, IOPMOD_EXPORT_MAGIC 0x41c00000, and IOPMOD_IMPORT_MAGIC 0x41e00000.

Independent local byte audit of all 166 import library records and 748 nonterminal stubs across 24 IRX modules: all 748 first words are 0x03e00008; all second-word opcodes are 9 (ADDIU); all rs and rt fields are 0; all 166 import terminator pairs are exactly (0,0); all 166 version words have high16=0. These are measured corpus values, not evidence about every external IRX.
14 tests pass. Mutation cases reject changed JR instruction, nonzero LI rs, nonzero partial terminator, nonzero high version bits, invalid LI opcode, unterminated tables, and bounds errors.

disposition: Apply the encoding checks only to the documented measured profile. Exact raw corpus counters independently support the chosen constraints; retain the parser's ET 0xff80 and catalog/relocation limits.
